person.name: Fergus Irvine
person.tagline: Commercial operator in financial services. I build the systems underneath the conversation.
person.intro: I manage a client book at a global bank and I build the tools that book runs on. Before banking I spent seven years at sea as a navigation officer on cruise ships. Most days I build with Claude: dashboards a bank desktop can open with nothing installed, research systems that run fifty agents at once, and test suites that are allowed to say no. This repo is the evidence: the builds, the data they run on, and what each one proved.

tracks.title: If you run a sales, account or partnerships team
tracks.lead: Start with the client-book dashboards. They are what my own book runs on, and the deck builder is the tool I would bring to a first customer meeting. Then the Merck and Pandion model for how I read a deal.

tracks.title: If you run solutions, deployment or forward-deployed work
tracks.lead: Start with the master build and the setup page: how the statistics are implemented, how the exports are engineered around a locked-down desktop, and how I run agents, tests and verification.

tracks.title: If you run product or strategy
tracks.lead: Start with the benchmark and explore tabs, then the negative results: a prediction engine that proved there was no edge, and a trading pipeline that killed ten strategies before any reached capital.

domains.title: Financial services and capital markets
domains.blurb: Built inside a global bank's securities-finance business, or from public filings.

projects.name: Client Book dashboards
projects.what: Four single-file browser dashboards for a securities-finance client book: the master Client Book Dashboard & Deck Builder, its client-facing release, an EMEA aged-receivables tracker and a no-install exposure explorer. No server, no install, no network call. Every byte of parsing, charting, statistics and PDF or PPTX export runs inside the browser on a locked-down bank desktop.
projects.proof: Three releases deployed globally. Master build v41 scores a client against peers on 13 similarity factors, answers five analyst questions on an explore surface, runs paired t-tests, an F-test and Granger-style lead-lag tests with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, and exports decks into the user's own PPTX template. Every demo figure was recomputed in Python and matched in the browser to the cent.

projects.name: Merck & Co / Pandion Therapeutics acquisition model
projects.what: A full M&A model of Merck's $1.85bn acquisition of Pandion Therapeutics, rebuilt from SEC filings and press releases: rNPV, sum of parts, comparables, precedents, football field, sources and uses, ASC 805 purchase price allocation, accretion and dilution, pro forma, synergies, sensitivities and scenarios.
projects.proof: 17 integrated tabs, 751 live formulas, zero errors, plus a six-slide deal book and a five-page methodology guide. The workbook was built by hand; the documents were AI-assisted. Public information only, not investment advice, not affiliated with either company.

domains.title: Personal quant and decision systems
domains.blurb: Built for myself and for friends, with test suites and the results they produced, flattering or not. The code is being prepared for publication after a secrets scan; the figures are from the suites as they stand.

projects.name: Trade Advisor
projects.what: Personal multi-horizon trade decision-support web app: intraday to multi-year horizons, each with its own evidence base, a recommendation contract with entry, stop, target and invalidation, and outcome tracking that scores every call it makes.
projects.proof: 18-agent research workflow (about 1.2M tokens) over an 82-source registry; a 17-check safety suite; live execution gated behind 8 independent checks and off by default. Paper first, fail closed.

projects.name: equity-advisor
projects.what: Python CLI for equity research and recommendations, reused as the valuation engine inside Trade Advisor.
projects.proof: 115 test functions across 31 files; coverage pushed from 79% to 85% before the live-recommendation gate was allowed to switch on.

projects.name: algo-trader-v3
projects.what: Systematic trading pipeline in five gated stages: hypothesis, signal research, build, paper incubation, live.
projects.proof: 129 tests and 28 architecture decision records. A hook blocks a stage from advancing unless the previous gate's artefact exists on disk and reads PASS. Kill scoreboard: more than ten candidate edges tested and killed before any reached capital.

projects.name: Football Predictor
projects.proof: 196 tests. Ranked probability score 0.2018 on unseen data across 15 leagues and 34,903 matches: a skilful model, and its own conclusion is that no exploitable edge exists against the betting market.

projects.name: ETF Investment Simulator
projects.what: Offline Monte Carlo investment simulator built for a friend, comparing 36 funds across UK brokers.
projects.proof: 100,000 simulation paths in a browser Web Worker with no server, and warnings about survivorship and recency bias written into the assumptions page.

in_preparation.title: In preparation
in_preparation.blurb: Sanitised versions of work from this autumn, each landing as its own page.
items: AI for ship operators: a feasibility study from a 51-agent research run, with its method and sources.
A command-and-control AI layer for passenger ships: concept note and the gated method behind it.
Records-first prospecting: the method and scoring rubric behind a prospect pack built from public carrier records.
Enterprise account plan: a template drawn from a private-credit account plan, with the firm removed.
Meeting-prep workspace: question bank, flashcards, side-by-side documents and notes, demonstrated on a fictional company.
Target-account research pipeline: API ingest, a classifier, embedding-similarity tiers and a live dashboard, on synthetic data.

build.title: How I build with Claude
summary: A Contabo VPS (12 vCPU, 47 GB RAM) runs headless Claude Code for agent fleets. The Mac stays master; cloud sessions take the overnight research.
A hook enforces a launch card before any agent run: three configurations, every model and effort level chosen fresh, usage share and finishing time stated. Nothing launches until I type go.
Finders write to disk, an independent verifier re-checks their claims, one judge decides. Briefs are files with an output schema.
Suites of 196, 129 and 115 tests; hook-enforced stage gates; a kill scoreboard; pre-registration and held-out controls on the models.
Single-file HTML tools for bank desktops, Python pipelines, React and Express on Render, artifacts with shared databases and per-user state.
One branch per task, draft PRs with a stated merge order, decision ids and version tags, HANDOVER and STATE files in every project.

proves: Deal mathematics and multi-agent research pipelines are the same discipline: state the claim, build the test, report the number.
The agent work here is shipped systems with governance in the tooling: launch cards, hooks, gates, allow-lists and kill scoreboards.
Negative results get the same care as positive ones. The prediction engine that found no edge is the project I would show first.
I can sit in front of the client and also ship the system underneath the conversation.
